Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, Chapter Two: It Runs in the Family

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} clan is less a clan than a family business with fangs. Membership divides sharply between unico sangue ("single blood") @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} — those both born into the mortal Giovanni family and Embraced into the clan — and doppio sangue ("double blooded") Kindred, Embraced into the clan without being born into the bloodline. The unico sangue consider themselves the natural aristocracy of the family and habitually place their own kin in positions of authority over more experienced or capable doppio sangue, a bias that causes constant, simmering resentment.

Anziani (Elders): The Giovanni elders, based largely out of the Mausoleum of the Giovanni in Venice, are split into two informal camps following the maelstrom that gutted the clan's stockpiled ghosts: the Anziani Prudente (Cautious Elders), who see opportunity in the weakened Shroud and newly created "buffet" fetters, and the Anziani Appasionati (Eager Elders), who want to actively foment mass-casualty violence (war, genocide, nuclear conflict) to manufacture more ghosts and accelerate the Endless Night.

The Proxy Kiss: Ghouls of the family are traditionally created through the Proxy Kiss, a ceremonial feeding of Giovanni vitae given to promising mortal cousins as a precursor to (and political test before) the Embrace. The practice inevitably creates a partial blood bond to the ghoul's domitor, which the anziani weigh heavily — along with generation, talent, genealogy, and gender bias — when deciding who may Embrace whom. The custom is observed most faithfully in Italy and is fading elsewhere, with the Milliners in particular treating it as optional.

Tithing: Giovanni of sufficient standing (or bound by a strict sire) are expected to tithe to the family, either in money or in properly imprisoned souls (requiring the fourth rank of Necromancy to hold a ghost at least a week). Typical tithes run from one soul for a dependent neonate up to five or seven for an independent, well-regarded Kindred; the anziani themselves capture far more than this routinely and do not tithe at all.

Client Families (Doppio Sangue Branches)

The Milliners: An American branch specializing in financial, legal, and criminal influence (organized crime infiltration, HMOs, privatized prisons, health policy manipulation). Despite delivering enormous material benefit to the clan, the Milliners receive little credit or reward from Venice, breeding deep resentment toward the unico sangue leadership, particularly Diego Giovanni.

The Dunsirn: A Scottish/northern European branch of financiers and robber barons, historically indifferent to Necromancy. Following the maelstrom, the anziani are pressuring Dunsirn neonates (and even older Dunsirn) to learn Necromancy so they can tithe in souls rather than money, a demand the proud Dunsirn deeply resent as it threatens their independence during the formative years of the European Union.

The Pisanob: A Mexican/Central American branch practicing a distinct, ritual-heavy strain of Necromancy derived from Aztec death-magic (see the Pisanob Necromancy rituals). Devastated by the maelstrom, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} incursions, mortal hunters, and conflict with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls}, the Pisanob organization is in disarray, though Pochtli's development of the Ritual of Pochtli may offer a path to recovery.

The della Passaglia: A merchant family whose decades of cultivating Cathayan (Kuei-jin) contacts in the East have collapsed disastrously, with former associates now hostile or violent.

The Putanesca: A minor family focused on murder, vice, and blackmail in Europe and North America, largely untouched by the maelstrom due to their general disinterest in Necromancy.

The Ghiberti: An African branch acquired via the 17th-century slave trade, who fused their prior trade knowledge with African necromantic traditions learned from indigenous practitioners to create the Cenotaph Path (see Necromancy: Cenotaph Path). Politically stable and prospering amid regional conflict, which supplies both blood and death-energy.

The Rosselini: Considered even by Giovanni standards to be needlessly cruel, pursuing Necromancy as an end in itself rather than a means to power. Their extreme, punishing treatment of summoned spirits has backfired since the Shroud thinned, turning many of their servants into vengeful spettri.

The Premascines

An uncertain legend among the Giovanni: a handful of ancient co-conspirators (numbers vary in the telling) who backed Augustus Giovanni's original diablerie of his sire in 1444 and allegedly still exist, hidden beneath the canals of Venice. If real, they are described as unfathomably powerful and versed in Necromancy beyond any modern ancilla, but too alien and isolated to serve as a practical resource for the clan — though some credit them with quietly protecting Venice from the worst of the post-maelstrom spirit unrest.
